key_insight: RetiJev directly scores predefined ophthalmic answers, improving benchmark accuracy while avoiding slower autoregressive generation.
clinical_relevance: Fast candidate scoring could support ophthalmic decision workflows, but benchmark results do not establish safety or effectiveness in patient care.
method: Builds source-grounded training data from PubMed Central articles, an eye-disease MeSH vocabulary, and 11 guideline-grading systems.
Trains 0.8B–9B models to score candidate answers without autoregressive decoding.
Compares performance with a 27B LLM and the commercial Jev 1.13 decision model.
evidence_signal: Using 128,232 training questions and a 24,662-question evaluation benchmark, RetiJev improved guideline-grading accuracy by 10.4–23.0 percentage points; RetiJev-9B answered cases in 158 ms on one GPU.
watch_item: The abstract does not report prospective clinical validation; performance on source-derived questions may not generalize to real-world patients.
paper_title: RetiJev: Fast and Source-Grounded Ophthalmic Decision Models
